draft.text:
{"letter":"Dear Priya Raman,

Two paddle festivals a year, a newsletter that goes out to a real community, and a social feed that sounds like the same friendly small company every day: that's the job Harpeth Outdoor Co. describes, and it's very close to the work I've done for community sports organizations over the past five years.

I got my start as a Marketing Assistant at Harpeth Valley Rec Center, where I wrote the weekly member newsletter for 3,000 subscribers. Writing something every single week for that many people teaches you to keep it clear and warm, and to make it worth opening. In the same role I coordinated volunteer schedules for 25 community events a year. That's a lot of shifts to fill and a lot of people to keep in the loop, and it's the part of event work I've come to enjoy most, because the day only goes well if the volunteers feel prepared.

Since 2021 I've been the Social Media Manager for Riverbend Youth Soccer League. I planned and ran a 40-team spring tournament with 600 attendees, which is probably the closest thing on my resume to a festival weekend. On the social side, I grew our Instagram following from 2,400 to 9,100 in two seasons, and I cut paid ad spend by 38% by shifting budget to player-made video. I keep our posting consistent with Hootsuite, and I make most of our graphics in Canva and Adobe Express, so keeping your channels looking and sounding like one brand is work I already do day to day.

What drew me to this posting is how clearly it reads like a company that cares about its community, right down to closing early on the first warm Friday of spring. I'd love to bring what I've learned running tournaments and volunteer crews to your spring and fall paddle festivals, and to get to know the people who show up for them. The hybrid setup in Franklin would also suit me well.

I'd be glad to talk about how I could help with the newsletter and the festival season ahead.

Thanks for your time,
Jordan Avery"}
